patch_description: The prior programs all bottleneck on calling the expensive full-schedule evaluator `get_opt_seq_cost` for every candidate move, limiting SA to a few thousand iterations. Inspired by the recommendation about incremental cost evaluation, this version exploits the workload's `get_incremental_seq_cost(txn, key_map, cost)` primitive (seen referenced in the earliest context program) to build a fast incremental evaluator: a sequence's cost is computed by threading a (key_map, cost) state through one incremental call per transaction. At startup we verify this incremental cost exactly matches `get_opt_seq_cost` on random permutations; if it does, all greedy construction and SA move evaluation use the fast path, giving roughly an order-of-magnitude more search iterations. The greedy constructor now evaluates **every** remaining candidate per step (previously only 10 random samples) since each evaluation is now cheap, yielding much better starting solutions. The SA then runs many more iterations with insertion/swap/segment moves, plus stagnation kicks reheating from the best solution. If the incremental API is unavailable or inconsistent, we fall back to the original evaluator so correctness is preserved.
